title: Job 37
paragraphs: ¹ At this, my heart pounds and leaps from its place. ² Listen — listen to the thunder of his voice, to the rumbling that rolls from his mouth. ³ He unleashes it across the whole sky; his lightning strikes to the ends of the earth. ⁴ After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back his bolts when his voice is heard. ⁵ God thunders with his voice marvelously; he does great things we cannot comprehend.

⁶ He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the shower of rain, 'Be a mighty downpour.' ⁷ He stops every person in their tracks, so that all people may know his work. ⁸ The animals find shelter and stay in their dens. ⁹ The storm sweeps in from the south; the cold comes from the driving north winds. ¹⁰ The breath of God produces ice, and the broad waters freeze solid.

¹¹ He loads the clouds with moisture; he scatters his lightning through them. ¹² They swirl around, guided by his purposes, doing all he commands over the face of the whole earth. ¹³ He brings the clouds either to punish the land, or to water it, or to show his love.

¹⁶ Do you know how the clouds are balanced — the wonderful work of him who is perfect in knowledge? ¹⁷ Do you know how your garments are warm when the earth lies still under the south wind? ¹⁸ Can you, with him, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of polished bronze? ¹⁹ Tell us what we should say to him — we cannot argue our case because of our darkness. ²⁰ Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone dare to ask to be swallowed up?

²¹ No one can look at the light when it blazes in the skies after the wind has swept them clear. ²² Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed in awesome majesty. ²³ The Almighty — we cannot find him; he is great in power. Justice and abundant righteousness he will not violate. ²⁴ Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own eyes."
